Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

an initialing formal ('this._home') to initialize the field •

- rename the field so the pattern does not fire, e.g. `String? _injectedHome;` assigned from `home`, or
- add `// ignore: prefer_initializing_formals` with a one-line comment explaining why the formal cannot be used.

CI runs `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings` for flutter_app, so this does not fail the build — filing as polish to keep the file lint-clean.

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/test/services/dap_home_test.dart` line 17

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the remaining branches of the `resolveDapHome` precedence contract**

The new tests cover two of the four contract branches: override + empty env (the Android shape) and explicit-home-wins. Two behaviorally important branches are unpinned:

1. **Override beats an ambient `HOME` env.** The production precedence works through `defaultDapConfigFile(home, environment)`: once `resolveDapHome` returns the sandbox path, a stray `HOME` in the process environment (e.g. a device/emulator where one exists, or a future platform regression) is bypassed.    test('override beats an ambient HOME in the environment', () async {
     final dir = await Directory.systemTemp.createTemp('dap_home');
     addTearDown(() => dir.delete(recursive: true));
     dapHomeOverride = dir.path;
     final svc = IoDapHubService(environment: {'HOME': '/nonexistent'});

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/

when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle/
          retention-days: 1

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the PTY legs are hosted-Linux ONLY. The audit of
  # the whole shard manifest (scripts/test_integration_shards.json) found
  # ZERO genuinely macOS-specific tests: the PTY harness allocates terminals
  # via libc openpty FFI (package:pty2 — OS/arch independent), no suite
  # depends on zsh defaults or /bin/bash 3.2 quirks, and the one macOS-only
  # assertion (fa_cube_integration_test.dart's SBPL kernel nested-rw probe)
  # is `if (Platform.isMacOS)`-guarded inside a test that passes on Linux.
  # The genuinely macOS-only terminal behavior keeps its dedicated gates:
  # cube-kernel-live (above) runs the real sandbox-exec E2E (test/cube/
  # backends) on fa-m5-1, and the mac-only CLI lines (shift_hid CoreGraphics
  # probe, stty -f device flag) stay unit-covered on ubuntu
  # (test/cli/shift_hid_test.dart, fa_tui_controller_overlay_test.dart).
  # Consequence: the fa-m5 runner-pick probe (M5_POOL) is GONE and the mac
  # leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_pty_coverage
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_pty_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.

blocks.text:
Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

- rename the field so the pattern does not fire, e.g. `String? _injectedHome;` assigned from `home`, or
- add `// ignore: prefer_initializing_formals` with a one-line comment explaining why the formal cannot be used.

CI runs `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings` for flutter_app, so this does not fail the build — filing as polish to keep the file lint-clean.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

The new tests cover two of the four contract branches: override + empty env (the Android shape) and explicit-home-wins. Two behaviorally important branches are unpinned:

     final dir = await Directory.systemTemp.createTemp('dap_home');
     addTearDown(() => dir.delete(recursive: true));
     dapHomeOverride = dir.path;
     final svc = IoDapHubService(environment: {'HOME': '/nonexistent'});

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}

      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)

        env:

          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
