Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. ## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

CI runs `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings` for flutter_app, so this does not fail the build — filing as polish to keep the file lint-clean.

The new tests cover two of the four contract branches: override + empty env (the Android shape) and explicit-home-wins. Two behaviorally important branches are unpinned:

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The doc says: "the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement, taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2... On x64 without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously."

This is the arm64 merged leg — coverage measurement is nondeterministic (PTY tests). The reviewer flagged this as a flaky/overdrafted ratchet: baseline sits < 0.1pp above a non-CI-condition run.

The ci_violations.json says owned = 0, unknown = 2 — so neither violation is attributed to a file in the diff. Per the general guidelines, when there's no owned table → FIX_CI "Fix CI root cause".

What's the right root-cause fix here? Options:

1. **Land terminal/PTY test coverage to restore margin** — add tests for lib/src/cli/** paths exercised by the PTY integration suites, raising measured coverage above the baseline. This is the "real" fix in spirit (ratchet only goes up).

2. **Re-measure/rebase the baseline via the coverage-gardener process** — but the ratchet says baseline only moves up. The current measured value is BELOW the baseline, so a gardener re-measure would not lower it. Actually wait — can it? "The baseline only ever moves UP — the weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it". So lowering the baseline is against the design.

Hmm, but the baseline was ratcheted to 18.42 in gh-1697/#1701. The measurement is nondeterministic because PTY tests on arm64 (or CI conditions) measure differently run-to-run. The margin is razor-thin: baseline 18.42 vs a plain x64 measurement of ~18.37.

Actually, wait. Let me think about what "merged shards" means: PTY coverage shards run on the CI leg with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 and get merged. The measured 18.31% is on the arm64 (or x64?) merged leg. The reviewer says "the baseline sits < 0.1 pp above a non-CI-condition run, so nondeterministic PTY coverage on the arm64 merged leg dips under".

So the root cause: the baseline is too tight relative to measurement noise. The genuinely correct fix given "ratchet only moves up" is to **increase actual coverage** by landing PTY/terminal tests covering uncovered CLI code paths. That both fixes the red gate robustly and increases margin against noise.

How much do we need? 18.42 - 18.31 = 0.11pp. What is the total DA line count in lib/src/cli/**? Let me compute: coverage % = hit/total. If total ≈ N lines, we need extra hits to move +0.11pp+. Let me compute from the numbers... I don't have the merged lcov locally, but I can compute the total from the repo: `find lib/src/cli -name '*.dart' | xargs wc -l`.

Let me look at the numbers: 18.31% measured. To get from 18.31% to ≥ 18.42% we need delta of 0.11pp. If total lines = T, then hits = 0.1831*T, need hits + h such that (hits+h)/T ≥ 0.1842, h ≥ 0.001*T. If T ≈ 20,000 lines, h ≈ 22 lines. So covering ~25-50 new lines would do it, but I want margin for noise (say target ≥ 18.6% locally... hmm, but local x64 measurement runs at ~18.37% while CI measured 18.31%).

Hmm wait, actually there's an important subtlety: can I even run the PTY coverage suite locally? It runs the integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests). That could take a while (the CI leg is the long one). Memory notes say long verification runs get killed by session restarts every 30-90 min, and to prefer short targeted tests + let branch-push validation CI run the full suite. The PTY coverage suite is probably 20+ minutes (3 shards merged). Risky but might be feasible in background.

Alternative cheaper approach: understand which files lib/src/cli are uncovered and add tests... but hold on — coverage of lib/src/cli is measured from PTY INTEGRATION suite tests (test/pty_integration? let me check). The coverage comes from running the PTY integration suites with coverage enabled, then merging lcov.

Let me look at how the CI workflow runs this to reproduce locally. Let me check .github/workflows for the PTY gates job.

Also there's the possibility that the coverage dipped because of something in the merged shards' nondeterminism (timing, PTY budget). The check at line 452: `expected 3 pty shard coverage reports` — shards 0,1,2 merged: 2285 files.

Approach decision: The cleanest durable fix consistent with the design (ratchet only up; do not touch baseline downward; can't rebase via gardener to a lower number) is to ADD terminal/PTY integration test coverage of lib/src/cli paths to push the measured value comfortably above the baseline. E.g. pick a CLI module with low coverage that's cheap to cover via existing PTY integration test patterns.

Let me explore: what does the PTY coverage run execute? Look at .github/workflows to find pty-coverage shards, and scripts to run them locally.

The nondeterminism: PTY tests are timing-sensitive; coverage depends on which code paths execute (timeouts, error paths, reconnects, etc.). The margin is 0.11pp.

---dart_test.yaml---
tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1730._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue

— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` line 76

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: hub credentials now ride the default iCloud backup on iOS**

This line redirects the `~/.dap` hub layout into `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/fah_sandbox/`. On iOS that is the app's `Documents/` directory, which iCloud device backup includes **by default** — nothing in `flutter_app/ios` sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`.

What lands there once a hub connection is saved:

- `.dap/config.json` — contains the hub `clientSecret`, which per this same file's doc the hub accepts **directly as a credential** (not a derived token);
- `.dap/keys/fah/<name>.key` — the agent identity key;
- `.dap/channels.json` — X25519 channel keypairs.

The repo has an explicit precedent for keeping secret stores out of device backups: issue #329 E4 excluded `fah_keychain.xml` from both `backup_rules.xml` (API ≤ 30) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer), with the rationale that key material must never leave the device. That exclusion does not cover this new file tree, so a hub credential that grants inbound access to the user's agent network will silently leave the device in every backup.

(On Android the picture is milder: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` resolves to `<dataDir>/app_flutter`, which falls outside the default Auto Backup domains of `files/`+`databases/`+`shared_prefs/` — so this is primarily the iOS leg.)

Suggested fix (small): mark the `.dap` directory excluded from backups on iOS right where it is created/redirected — e.g. set the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` URL resource key on the sandbox `.dap` subtree (or persist under a directory excluded by policy) — mirroring the #329 E4 intent. If shipping the credential in cloud backup is a deliberate product decision, please say so in the PR description; as written it reads as an unreviewed side effect of the storage-location fix.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.

Note: the baseline value is the pty-integration-linux CI leg's measurement,
taken with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 (the leg's 2x PTY budget stretch). On x64
without that scale the same tree measures ~18.37% — below the committed
floor — so a plain local run fails the gate spuriously. Reproduce the CI
measurement with FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 before suspecting a regression.
The baseline file itself must stay a bare number: both this script and
coverage-gardener.yml parse it with float().
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime

    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
