`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal
       (OPENAI/OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE/GEMINI/OLLAMA/GROQ/MISTRAL/
       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or
       loopback marker (`MockLlmServer`, `MockOpenAiServer`, `127.0.0.1`,
       `localhost`): injecting a dummy key to drive key resolution against
       a loopback mock is the standard deterministic pattern (see
       fa_cube_headless_helper.scrubbedChildEnv).

Scope (gh-1199 AC2): only files tagged `integration` WITHOUT the `llm`
tag are checked — those are the only files that can join the deterministic
integration gate (shard_files.py --tags integration). Unit suites never
carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot
flake the merge; flagging them would only pin noise. The `llm`-tagged
files are the audited `live` class; everything integration-tagged that
passes these markers is `mock` by construction.

A flagged file that is genuinely deterministic must be pinned in
AUDIT_MOCK below with a one-line justification; the list is part of the
PR review surface (gh-1199 AC3 — every entry is an audited `mock`
classification).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal
       (OPENAI/OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE/GEMINI/OLLAMA/GROQ/MISTRAL/
       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or
       loopback marker (`MockLlmServer`, `MockOpenAiServer`, `127.0.0.1`,
       `localhost`): injecting a dummy key to drive key resolution against
       a loopback mock is the standard deterministic pattern (see
       fa_cube_headless_helper.scrubbedChildEnv).

Scope (gh-1199 AC2): only files tagged `integration` WITHOUT the `llm`
tag are checked — those are the only files that can join the deterministic
integration gate (shard_files.py --tags integration). Unit suites never
carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot
flake the merge; flagging them would only pin noise. The `llm`-tagged
files are the audited `live` class; everything integration-tagged that
passes these markers is `mock` by construction.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal

       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or

       `localhost`): injecting a dummy key to drive key resolution against
       a loopback mock is the standard deterministic pattern (see
       fa_cube_headless_helper.scrubbedChildEnv).

tag are checked — those are the only files that can join the deterministic
integration gate (shard_files.py --tags integration). Unit suites never
carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot
flake the merge; flagging them would only pin noise. The `llm`-tagged
files are the audited `live` class; everything integration-tagged that
passes these markers is `mock` by construction.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the

  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from

  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes

- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):

  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal
       (OPENAI/OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE/GEMINI/OLLAMA/GROQ/MISTRAL/
       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or
       loopback marker (`MockLlmServer`, `MockOpenAiServer`, `127.0.0.1`,
       `localhost`): injecting a dummy key to drive key resolution against
       a loopback mock is the standard deterministic pattern (see
       fa_cube_headless_helper.scrubbedChildEnv).

Scope (gh-1199 AC2): only files tagged `integration` WITHOUT the `llm`
tag are checked — those are the only files that can join the deterministic
integration gate (shard_files.py --tags integration). Unit suites never
carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot
flake the merge; flagging them would only pin noise. The `llm`-tagged
files are the audited `live` class; everything integration-tagged that
passes these markers is `mock` by construction.

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the

  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal

       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or
       loopback marker (`MockLlmServer`, `MockOpenAiServer`, `127.0.0.1`,

carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes

  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`

- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the

join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,
       api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai, chatgpt.com, api.z.ai);
    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal
       (OPENAI/OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE/GEMINI/OLLAMA/GROQ/MISTRAL/
       DEEPSEEK/GLM/ZAI/CODEGPT/COPILOT/CHATGPT/... + _API_KEY/_TOKEN/
       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or
       loopback marker (`MockLlmServer`, `MockOpenAiServer`, `127.0.0.1`,
       `localhost`): injecting a dummy key to drive key resolution against
       a loopback mock is the standard deterministic pattern (see
       fa_cube_headless_helper.scrubbedChildEnv).

Scope (gh-1199 AC2): only files tagged `integration` WITHOUT the `llm`
tag are checked — those are the only files that can join the deterministic
integration gate (shard_files.py --tags integration). Unit suites never
carry secrets into their legs, so a key-naming unit fixture there cannot
flake the merge; flagging them would only pin noise. The `llm`-tagged
files are the audited `live` class; everything integration-tagged that
passes these markers is `mock` by construction.

A flagged file that is genuinely deterministic must be pinned in
AUDIT_MOCK below with a one-line justification; the list is part of the
PR review surface (gh-1199 AC3 — every entry is an audited `mock`
classification).

7:two budgets against the committed baseline (test_duration_baseline.json):

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes

- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,

  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

All 3 open review threads fixed in code, plus the red pre-merge CI gate rooted at the PTY coverage ratchet. Head pushed: `975331175a`.

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure root cause (2 failing checks, both from one red):** `PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)` failed with `CLI coverage 18.31% regressed below baseline 18.42%`; `Quality gate` is the aggregator that follows it. `ci_violations.json` marks both `ownership: unknown` (no attributable `path:line` — the PR diff touches only `flutter_app/`, never `lib/src/cli/**`). - **Root-cause fix instead of a re-roll:** neither `--output-format stream-json` (issue #695) nor `--output events` (issue #155) had any integration-taged suite, so the headless event writers measured 0% on exactly the leg that feeds the `lib/src/cli` ratchet. New `test/integration/headless_event_streams_test.dart` covers both writers through the real `AgentCli.runHeadless` and follows the repo precedent of raising real coverage instead of touching the baseline (ratchet stays "only up"; no baseline edit).
- **Measured effect:** merging the new suite's coverage with the failed run's three shard artifacts: `+206` `lib/src/cli` line hits → `18.31% → 19.27%`, a ~0.85pp guard band over the 18.42 floor.
- **Inherited-tree note:** the auto-save bot's branch sync merged `main` (store-appearance fix + message-cap tests) into this branch mid-rework; those files are not part of this rework's changes.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN) per finding:

1. **IMPORTANT — hub credentials rode the default iCloud backup on iOS** (`env_factory_io.dart:76`): wrote the failing env-factory tests first (`.dap` creation + exclusion request recorded through a test seam), then implemented — eager `<sandbox>/.dap` creation + `excludePathFromBackup()`; new `fah/icloud` `excludeFromBackup` native method sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` on the directory and its existing descendants (upgrade-safe). Only `.dap` is excluded; sessions/apps stay restorable.
2. **SUGGESTION — `prefer_initializing_formals`** (`dap_service_io.dart:30`): reproduced with `flutter analyze`, then applied the reviewer's first resolution — field `_home` → `_injectedHome` (the public `home:` named parameter is unchanged); analyzer no longer reports the info.
3. **SUGGESTION — pin the `resolveDapHome` precedence contract** (`dap_home_test.dart`): added the two missing pins — override beats an ambient `HOME` (with a negative write assertion, through `defaultDapConfigFile`) and no-override/no-injected-home → null — plus the mutable-global ordering doc on `dapHomeOverride`.
4. **CI gate** as described above (RED = the ratchet leg itself; the new suite turns it GREEN with margin).

- `flutter_app/lib/services/backup_exclusion.dart` (new) — iOS backup-exclusion channel wrapper + test seam.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/env_factory_io.dart` — eager `.dap` creation + exclusion before the shell loads.

- `flutter_app/lib/services/dap_service_io.dart` — `_injectedHome` rename (lint), doc note.
- `flutter_app/lib/services/dap_home.dart` — ordering doc on `dapHomeOverride`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-provider tag-boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2/AC3).

The merge-blocking Quality gate is deterministic-only: every test that
performs live provider I/O must carry the `llm` tag (and is then excluded
from every per-PR leg by `--exclude-tags llm` / shard_files.py
`--exclude-tag llm`). This lint makes the boundary self-enforcing: a test
file that LOOKS live fails the gate, so a new live test can never silently
join the gate again ("raz i navsegda").

Markers (comments stripped before matching; string literals are what
count — same discipline as shard_files.file_has_tag, with `https://`
spared inside literals):
    1. a real provider base URL as a string literal
       (openrouter.ai, anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openai.azure.com,
       generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.groq.com, api.mistral.ai,
       api.deepseek.com, ollama.com, api.x.ai, api.cohere.ai,

    2. a concrete provider credential env key as a string literal

       _SECRET/_CREDENTIALS) — only counts when the file shows no mock or

  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.

  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First

  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow

  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
